sections.html:
Bellevue is the oldest community in Nebraska and sits in Sarpy County, just south of Omaha. The census counted 50,137 residents in 2010 and 64,176 in 2020. Its land area grew from 15.85 square miles in 2010 to 21.13 in 2020, so a house on the newer edge of town can be in a very different neighborhood from one near the old center, even though both carry a Bellevue address.

Most homes are owner-occupied, and 86.8 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. That is typical of an established city, and it leaves a steady supply of long-held houses that may need updating before a traditional listing.

sections.h2: Offutt Air Force Base and your timeline
sections.html:
Offutt Air Force Base, just outside town, shapes who buys and sells in Bellevue. It began as Fort Crook, an Army post from the 1890s, was named Offutt Field on May 6, 1924, and became Strategic Air Command headquarters on November 9, 1948. Today it is the home of the 55th Wing, with U.S. Strategic Command on base. The base counts a combined military and civilian workforce of roughly 12,000 and more than 22,000 family members. The 2019 flood destroyed about a third of the base, and the rebuild of the southeastern part was scheduled to wrap up around 2027.

Military households move on orders, not on a seller's preferred schedule. A Bellevue owner who gets reassigned, inherits a house, or cannot rent it out may need a fast close that does not depend on a buyer's loan approval.

Property tax for Bellevue comes from Sarpy County, so the county Treasurer, Assessor and Clerk are who you deal with, and city hall is not. The Treasurer's Office occupies the 1102 Building, 1102 E. 1st Street in Papillion. Lines grow longest from 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m., all day Fridays, and on the first and last day of any month, so schedule a payoff question for another time if you can.

The protest window runs June 1 through June 30 each year. Owners whose value changed get a goldenrod yellow postcard. A protest uses Form 422, filed with the County Clerk at 1210 Golden Gate Drive in Papillion. File in person by 4:45 p.m. on June 30, online by 11:59 p.m., or by mail postmarked by June 30. A postal drop-box does not guarantee a same-day postmark, so have mail postmarked at a post office counter.

If you think a value is too high before you list, plan around that June window, not around your closing date.

sections.h2: Selling a house in poor condition
sections.html:
Chapter 15 of the Bellevue Code of Ordinances gives the Permits and Inspections Department authority to inspect dwellings and to placard one as unfit for human habitation. A seller with a damaged or neglected property should know how the process runs, because it affects both value and timing.

  • Section 15-21 lets the department enter and inspect dwellings at reasonable times, and owners or occupants must give access.
  • Section 15-24 gives a person who receives a notice ten days to file a written petition for a hearing. Without one, the notice automatically becomes an order.
  • Section 15-29 lists the defects that support an unfit placard, including a dwelling that is dilapidated, unsanitary, difficult to heat, unsafe or vermin infested.
  • Section 15-34 bars a placarded home from being lived in again until the department removes the placard in writing.
  • Section 15-36 prohibits gas or electric service to a placarded dwelling except for authorized repairs.
  • Section 15-37 creates a five-member Board of Housing Appeals to hear appeals from department decisions.

The city's Code Enforcement Unit enforces city codes and zoning ordinances in Bellevue and its zoning jurisdiction. Under section 15-35, tenants of a placarded building owe no rent from the date the placard goes up, so an owner with renters should move quickly on any notice.

Bellevue Public Schools is the main district. It serves about 10,000 students and lists two high schools, three middle schools, 15 elementary schools, one alternative school and a career and technical education center. Buyers with children often ask which elementary and middle school an address feeds, so have your exact street address ready and confirm attendance areas with the district rather than guess.

Ask the Sarpy County Treasurer for the balance on your parcel and give it to the title company, which pays it from your proceeds. Sarpy follows the larger-county calendar, so tax is delinquent earlier than in most of the state. Ask what is already due if you sell in spring.

sections.h2: What a Bellevue seller pays at closing
sections.html:
Nebraska's documentary stamp tax lands on the seller, and section 76-901 puts it at $3.32 per $1,000 of value on transfers before January 1, 2032.

State law also makes sellers of homes with one to four units give buyers a written condition statement (section 76-2,120). It spans appliances, electrical, heating and cooling, water, sewer, hazards and title matters such as easements. Should something change before the buyer is bound, you must update it.

  • Collect a payoff letter for each mortgage or lien.
  • Find out from the title company how this year's property tax gets divided.
  • Assemble the condition statement before any buyer asks for it.

Paying cash means no mortgage, so no lender appraisal and no loan committee to wait for. That suits a Bellevue owner who needs a firm date, whether a reassignment, an inheritance or a rental that no longer earns its keep.

Tax payoff, stamp tax and condition statement stay on your plate. The clock, though, rests on title work and your own paperwork.

Bellevue sellers can head off most buyer questions with a short folder. Put in a payoff letter, the written condition statement, any repair invoices, and notes on the school attendance area for your street. If the house is rented, add the lease and the dates of any inspections. If the city has ever sent a notice about the property, have a copy of it and of how it was resolved.

A buyer who sees that paperwork up front tends to ask fewer questions later, which helps the closing stay on schedule.

faqs.q: Which county do I deal with when selling a house in Bellevue?
faqs.a: Sarpy County. Bellevue property tax is billed and collected by the Sarpy County Treasurer in Papillion, and valuation protests are filed with the Sarpy County Clerk.

faqs.q: Can the city of Bellevue condemn a house in bad shape?
faqs.a: Yes, through a defined process. Under Chapter 15 of the city code, the Permits and Inspections Department can placard a dwelling as unfit and serve a notice. An owner can petition for a hearing within ten days of a notice.

faqs.q: How much is Nebraska deed stamp tax on a Bellevue sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays $3.32 for each $1,000 of value, or fraction of $1,000, for transfers before January 1, 2032.

faqs.q: When is the property valuation protest deadline in Sarpy County?
faqs.a: The protest period runs June 1 through June 30 each year. Form 422 goes to the Sarpy County Clerk, in person by 4:45 p.m. on June 30, online by 11:59 p.m., or by mail postmarked on or before June 30.

faqs.q: Does the Offutt base affect how fast Bellevue homes sell?
faqs.a: It shapes the buyer and seller pool, since the base has a workforce of roughly 12,000. Families who move on orders often need a firm closing date.
